result.topic_en: This is a draft for Riemann's dissertation. It shows that the boundary integral $\int (X\,dx/dp + Y\,dy/dp)\,ds$ around an isolated discontinuity point vanishes when $\varrho X$ and $\varrho Y$ become infinitely small, by bounding the integral over a small circle by $K/2\pi$. Section IV states that if the integral vanishes over every bounding curve, its value along a line from $O_0$ to $O$ is independent of the path.

methods.what: Boundary integral around an isolated discontinuity point, evaluated on a small circle of radius $\varrho$ in polar coordinates
Estimate: if the integrand times $\varrho$ is less than $K/2\pi$ for every angle, the integral over the circle is less than $K$, which contradicts a nonzero value $K$
Path independence of the line integral when its integral around every bounding curve vanishes

items.english: With respect to the boundary of a mere discontinuity point, the integral cannot take a value different from zero if $\varrho X$ and $\varrho Y$ become infinitely small with the distance $\varrho$ of the point O from it.

items.english: If, in a two-dimensionally extended surface spread over A, the integral is zero with respect to every part of the surface, then for any two fixed points $O_0$ and $O$ the integral taken along any line from $O_0$ to $O$ always has the same value.
